title: Same-Day Pizza Dough
subtitle: A quick pizza dough ready to use in 2 to 3 hours
excerpt: Same-day pizza dough uses a higher proportion of yeast and a warm prove to give a workable dough in 2 to 3 hours. It is less complex in flavour than a cold-proved dough but produces a good pizza when there is no time to plan ahead. The dough works best at high heat with a pizza stone.
sourceNotes: Same-day pizza dough is a modern home-baking adaptation of Neapolitan pizza dough method, adjusting yeast quantities for a short warm prove. Traditional Neapolitan dough uses a 24-hour or longer cold prove; the same-day version trades some flavour depth for convenience.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze proved and shaped dough balls in individual bags. Defrost at room temperature for 2 hours before using.
recipe.batchNotes: Dough scales in exact proportion. Make a double batch and freeze half.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made the same day (2 to 3 hour prove) or cold-proved for up to 3 days in the fridge.
recipe.temperatureNote: maximum oven temperature, pizza stone or steel

content.text: Same-day pizza dough is made with more yeast than a cold-proved dough and proves in a warm place for 2 to 3 hours rather than overnight. It makes a good pizza: not quite as flavoursome or as easy to stretch as a 48-hour cold-proved dough, but perfectly workable for a weeknight pizza. The same recipe can also be cold-proved in the fridge for 24 to 3 days if you plan ahead.

items.prepNote: 1 sachet (for same-day); use 2 g for cold prove

content.text: Combine the flour and salt in a large bowl. Mix in the yeast. Make a well in the centre and pour in the warm water and olive oil. Mix to a rough dough with your hands or a wooden spoon.

Turn out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8 to 10 minutes until the dough is smooth, slightly tacky, and elastic. It should spring back when poked with a finger. If it tears when pulled, it needs more kneading.
Form the dough into a smooth ball, place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp cloth or cling film, and leave in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours until doubled in size.

Turn out and divide into 4 equal pieces (about 210 g each). Shape each into a tight ball by pulling the surface of the dough under itself. Place on a lightly oiled tray, cover, and rest for 30 minutes at room temperature before shaping.

On a well-floured surface, use your hands or a rolling pin to stretch or roll each ball to a 28 to 30 cm round. Same-day dough can be stiffer and more prone to springing back than cold-proved dough: if it resists, cover and rest for 5 minutes before trying again.
Top and bake on a preheated pizza stone at 250°C fan for 7 to 10 minutes until the base is crisp and the topping is cooked.

items.symptom: Dough springs back when shaped and won't hold its shape
items.cause: The gluten network is too tight: the dough needs more rest
items.fix: Cover the shaped dough and leave it for 5 to 10 minutes. The gluten will relax and the dough will be easier to stretch.

items.cause: Prove environment is too cool, or the yeast was old
items.fix: Move to a warmer spot: near a preheating oven or in a turned-off oven with just the light on. Check the yeast is in-date.

items.cause: Under-kneaded or over-proved, or a weak flour
items.fix: Knead thoroughly until the dough passes the 'windowpane' test: a small piece stretched between your fingers should thin enough to be translucent without tearing.

content.text: Traditional Neapolitan pizza dough uses a 24-hour cold prove with a small amount of yeast. This builds a complex, slightly tangy flavour that is hard to copy in a same-day dough. The same-day version is a home compromise. It is slightly denser and less stretchy, but it is ready within a few hours and good for an everyday pizza night.
